title: The universal unramified and injective parameter locus for algebraic spaces
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Work with algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], with sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] and the point spaces of [def-a1-space-point-topology]. Local finite type and unramifiedness mean the chart test of [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties] applied to the scheme properties [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and [def-weil-unramified-morphism], respectively. Universally injective means injective on point spaces after every algebraic-space base change. Let $p:A\to B$, $q:C\to B$, and $f:A\to C$ satisfy $q\circ f=p$. Suppose that $p$ is locally of finite type, and that $p$ and $p_2=p\circ\operatorname{pr}_1:A\times_C A\to B$ are closed maps on point spaces, meaning that they send closed subsets to closed subsets. Then there exists an open subspace $V\subseteq B$ [def-a1-space-open-subspace] such that, for every algebraic space $T$ over $S$ and every $h:T\to B$, the induced map $f_T:A\times_B T\to C\times_B T$ is unramified and universally injective if and only if $h$ factors through $V\hookrightarrow B$.

source.place: Tag 05X9 (spaces-more-morphisms-lemma-where-unramified-universally-injective), all three hypotheses and arbitrary algebraic-space parameter changes.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-closed-source-unramified-base-open] to the given triangle. Its hypotheses are precisely local finite type and closedness of $p$. Obtain an open $B_0\subseteq B$ such that, for every algebraic-space $h:T\to B$, $f_T$ is unramified exactly when $h$ factors through $B_0$. Put $A_0=A\times_BB_0$, $C_0=C\times_BB_0$, and $f_0=f_{B_0}$. Taking $h:B_0\hookrightarrow B$ shows that $f_0$ is unramified.

Put $D=A\times_C A$. The fibre-product universal property gives $D_0:=A_0\times_{C_0}A_0\simeq D\times_BB_0$, compatibly with the two projections and the diagonal: on every test scheme both sides are pairs $(a_1,a_2)$ with $f(a_1)=f(a_2)$ and their common $B$-coordinate in $B_0$. By [lem-a1-space-open-factor-scheme-tests], $D_0$ has point set $|p_2|^{-1}(|B_0|)$. By [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus], the open subspaces $D_0\subseteq D$ and $B_0\subseteq B$ have point spaces homeomorphic to these open subsets of $|D|$ and $|B|$. The restricted $r:D_0\to B_0$ is closed. Indeed any relatively closed $F\subseteq|D_0|$ is $F^\prime\cap |p_2|^{-1}(|B_0|)$ for some closed $F^\prime\subseteq|D|$, and $r(F)=p_2(F^\prime)\cap |B_0|$, closed in $|B_0|$. This uses the assumed closedness only for the original $p_2$, followed by restriction to an open base.

source.place: Tag 05X9, restriction to the unramified open does not destroy closedness; explicit relative-topology calculation.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-unramified-diagonal-open] to $f_0$. Identify $\Delta_{f_0}:A_0\to D_0$ with the open subspace $J\subseteq D_0$. By [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus], $|J|$ is an open subset of $|D_0|$, so its complement $E=|D_0|\setminus |J|$ is a closed subset. Since $r$ is closed, $O=|B_0|\setminus r(E)$ is open. Choose a scheme atlas of $B_0$ as in [def-trf-algebraic-space]; [lem-a1-space-invariant-open-quotient] applied to $O$ constructs an open subspace $V\subseteq B_0$ with point image $O$. Its composite inclusion into $B$ is open: on any scheme test it is a composite of inclusions of open subschemes. Thus it gives the required kind of open subspace of $B$.

source.place: Tag 05X9, open diagonal (Tag 05W1) and the closed-image-complement formula for W (Tag 03BZ).

proof.text: For $h:T\to B_0$, the same test-scheme description of pairs identifies $A_T\times_{C_T}A_T$ with $D_T=D_0\times_{B_0}T$ and its diagonal with the pullback of $J\hookrightarrow D_0$. Its point image is the inverse image of $|J|$ under $\pi:|D_T|\to|D_0|$, by [lem-a1-space-open-factor-scheme-tests]. This diagonal is surjective on points exactly when no point of $D_T$ maps into $E$. By the point-lifting assertion of [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus], a point of $E$ over $h(t)$ lifts to $D_T$ for every $t\in|T|$ above it. Conversely any such lift projects to that point of $E$ and to a $t$. Hence the diagonal is surjective exactly when $h(|T|)\cap r(E)=\varnothing$, equivalently $h(|T|)\subseteq O$, equivalently $h$ factors through $V$ by open factorization. No closedness after arbitrary base change is used.

source.place: Tag 05X9, final point-lifting square (Tag 03H4) and factorization through an open (Tag 03IE), applied to an arbitrary parameter space.

proof.text: For any map $g:X\to Y$ of algebraic spaces, its diagonal is surjective on points if and only if $g$ is universally injective. Here is the argument directly from the cited fibre-product and point calculus. If $g$ is universally injective, $\operatorname{pr}_1:X\times_YX\to X$ is injective on points. For $d\in|X\times_YX|$, the points $d$ and $\Delta_g(\operatorname{pr}_1(d))$ have the same first projection, so they are equal. Conversely suppose $|\Delta_g|$ is surjective. The point-lifting formula shows that every base change of $\Delta_g$ is also surjective. For any $Y^\prime\to Y$, the diagonal of $g^\prime:X^\prime\to Y^\prime$ is such a base change by the fibre-product universal property. Given $x_1,x_2\in|X^\prime|$ with the same image in $|Y^\prime|$, point lifting supplies $d\in|X^\prime\times_{Y^\prime}X^\prime|$ with these projections. Lift $d$ through the surjective diagonal; both projections of a diagonal point coincide, so $x_1=x_2$. This proves injectivity for every algebraic-space test.

source.place: Tag 040X (lemma-universally-injective), equivalence (2)--(3); the short proof is written out using Tag 03H4 rather than adding a duplicate of the general stack criterion.

proof.text: Let now $h:T\to B$ be arbitrary. If $f_T$ is unramified and universally injective, step 1 factors $h$ through $B_0$, uniquely since it is a subfunctor. Step 5 makes its diagonal surjective, and step 4 factors this map through $V\subseteq B_0$. Conversely if $h$ factors through $V$, it factors through $B_0$, so step 1 gives unramifiedness; step 4 gives surjectivity of its diagonal and step 5 gives universal injectivity. The identifications of step 2 show that these are the same induced map $f_T$ as in the statement. This establishes the equivalence for every $T$ and $h$, including the empty parameter space.

source.place: Tag 05X9, assembly of both implications after restoring the original base.

proof_origin.place: Tag 05X9 (lemma-where-unramified-universally-injective); expanded point arguments from Tags 03H4, 03IE and 040X.

lean.statement: theorem exists_openSubspace_unramified_radicial_parameter {S : Scheme.{u}} (A C B : AlgebraicSpace S) (p : A ⟶ B) (q : C ⟶ B) (f : A ⟶ C) (w : f ≫ q = p) (hp_lft : MapIsLocally (@LocallyOfFiniteType) p) (hp_closed : ∀ Z : Set (Point A.obj.obj), IsClosed Z → IsClosed {y : Point B.obj.obj | ∃ a : PointRepresentative A.obj.obj, (Quot.mk _ a : Point A.obj.obj) ∈ Z ∧ (Quot.mk _ (a.map p.hom.hom) : Point _) = y}) (hp2_closed : ∀ Z : Set (Point (Limits.pullback f.hom f.hom).obj), IsClosed Z → IsClosed {y : Point B.obj.obj | ∃ d : PointRepresentative (Limits.pullback f.hom f.hom).obj, (Quot.mk _ d : Point (Limits.pullback f.hom f.hom).obj) ∈ Z ∧ (Quot.mk _ (d.map ((pullback.fst f.hom f.hom) ≫ p.hom).hom) : Point _) = y}) : ∃ V : OpenSubspace B, ∀ (T : AlgebraicSpace S) (h : T ⟶ B), (MapIsLocally (@IsUnramified) (parameterBaseChangeMap p q f w h) ∧ ∀ (Y : AlgebraicSpace S) (g : Y ⟶ parameterBaseChange q h) (a b : PointRepresentative (Limits.pullback (parameterBaseChangeMap p q f w h).hom g.hom).obj), (Quot.mk _ (a.map (pullback.snd (parameterBaseChangeMap p q f w h).hom g.hom).hom) : Point Y.obj.obj) = Quot.mk _ (b.map (pullback.snd (parameterBaseChangeMap p q f w h).hom g.hom).hom) → (Quot.mk _ a : Point (Limits.pullback (parameterBaseChangeMap p q f w h).hom g.hom).obj) = Quot.mk _ b) ↔ ∃ l : T.obj.obj ⟶ V.val.toFunctor, l ≫ V.val.ι = h.hom.hom
